thread:
maria_support: Customer report — promo code 'TRIAL-JUNE2026' returns invalid/expired when applied via API. Dashboard shows it as active for the org. Customer id: org_8421, email: user+trial@example.com. They tried web checkout and our POST /v1/promos/apply curl and got 400.

maria_support: Paste of curl & response: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/promos/apply \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '{"code":"TRIAL-JUNE2026","org_id":"org_8421"}'
```
Response: 
```json
{ "error": { "type": "promo_invalid", "reason": "expired", "code": "PROMO_EXPIRED" }, "request_id": "req_9af3b1" }
```

maria_support: Customer says dashboard UI shows expiry "June 30 23:59 PDT" (they sent screenshot). They said they copied code from marketing email. Escalating because dashboard/admin shows active.

jonathan_dev: Thanks — can you paste the full request_id and server response headers (x-request-id etc)? Also which region/console the customer looked at?

maria_support: request_id=req_9af3b1, x-request-id: rwd-5b7c, user-agent: Redwood-CLI/2.1. Screenshot shows dashboard region US-WEST (PDT).

jonathan_dev: Reproduced locally with the same org_id. Hitting internal admin: GET /internal/promos/TRIAL-JUNE2026 returns metadata. Snip: 
```json
{ "code": "TRIAL-JUNE2026", "created_by": "marketing_app", "expires_at": "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z", "expires_tz": "America/Los_Angeles" }
```
jonathan_dev: Hmm — expires_at is stored as 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z which effectively makes it unavailable for PDT users on 2026-05-31 17:00 PDT. Dashboard apparently displays local end-of-day (June 30) using expires_tz but the API compare uses expires_at (UTC) directly. Looks like a mismatch between how UI calculates end-of-day and how backend enforces expiry.

sasha_billing: Looking at promo creation logs — these codes were imported by the marketing CSV on 2026-05-01. The CSV had expiry as "2026-06-30" (no time). Import routine previously set expiry to end-of-day in provided timezone, but last migration (promo service refactor) normalized dates to UTC midnight without converting day-of-day offsets. That would explain shift.

deploy-bot: Deploy event: promo-service v3.4.0 rolled at 2794509000 — change: "normalize expiry field to iso-utc without timezone conversion". Ticket: INF-4723.

jonathan_dev: OK that's the regression. For codes imported without an explicit time we now ended up with 00:00Z of the day instead of 23:59 local. That makes some codes expire ~16-24 hours earlier depending on TZ.

maria_support: Immediate ask from customer: can we grant credits or reissue extended code? They already lost application. Customer is on a paid plan trial conversion — high priority.

sasha_billing: I can apply a manual credit for org_8421 for the equivalent of the promo value. Doing now and will log invoice note.

sasha_billing: Manual credit applied: credit_9921, amount: $150, note: "manual compensation for promo expiry mismatch (INF-4723)". Notified customer by email.

maria_support: Sent customer confirmation, they accepted the manual credit and asked for a replacement promo code they can try.

jonathan_dev: Quick temporary workaround: we can allow a grace check in the apply endpoint to accept codes where expires_tz matches and date equals local end-of-day. But that's risky to hotpatch. Better: reissue a replacement code scoped to org_8421. I can create one now.

jonathan_dev: Created replacement code 'TRIAL-JUNE2026-EXT' valid until 2026-06-30T23:59:59 America/Los_Angeles. Applied to org_8421. Please test.

maria_support: Customer tested in chat — apply success, no error. They confirmed they can proceed. :white_check_mark:

jonathan_dev: I'll open a PR to fix the import/migration path so that when expiry is provided as a date (no time) we set expires_at to 23:59:59 in the provided timezone and store correct UTC. Also add a regression test. PR: github.com/redwood/proxy/pull/583 (WIP).

deploy-bot: Created issue INF-4723 -> fix scheduled for 2794518000 (next sprint).

sasha_billing: Recording manual credit and replacement code in billing notes and incident log. WillSurface to legal if customers request mass reissue.

maria_support: Closing this thread for org_8421 — customer satisfied. Follow-ups: jonathan please link PR when ready and we can consider batch reissue for all affected promo imports.

jonathan_dev: Will do. Thanks team. :raised_hands:

maria_support: Closing.
